reader_products.name: ShelfMates
reader_products.core_message: We don't just market books. We build reader relationships.
reader_products.role_in_system: [extrapolated] Retain/Repeat stage infrastructure — converts one-time video viewers or preorder buyers into an author's own reader list, then feeds retargeting and newsletter features off that list. Discovery -> reader relationship -> future releases.

reader_products.name: StoryPals
reader_products.core_message: We don't just market books. We build reader relationships.
reader_products.role_in_system: [extrapolated] Same retain/repeat function as ShelfMates, scoped to the children's/family genre segment rather than adult fiction.

hierarchy.business_result: e.g. measurable sales/KU/download movement — must not imply impressions = sales (PRD Section 15)

case_studies.note: Deferred by decision — case studies are intentionally left empty for this build pass, not a gap to be extrapolated. Keep the schema in place for when real client case-study data becomes available; this remains a blocker for Step 9 (Results/Catalogue pages) until then.

results.a: [extrapolated] Results build over the 90-day cycle: the first 30 days establish the system and baseline metrics, days 31-60 build momentum and strengthen social proof, and days 61-90 measure against baseline and identify what's working. Meaningful, sustained movement is more realistic by month 3 than month 1 — see the 90-Day Journey section.

results.q: What happens during the first month?
results.a: [extrapolated] We establish positioning, prepare content and creative assets, begin discovery-stage posting, and set the baseline metrics everything else gets measured against.

No. We don't guarantee a specific number of sales, a category ranking, or a bestseller position — publishing and reader behavior don't work that way. What we guarantee is that we'll do the agreed work; see the Atomic Shelf Commitment for exactly what that covers.

[extrapolated] Depends on your plan's stage: content-only plans report impressions, video views, click-throughs, and sales lift; campaign plans (Momentum/Growth) also report preorders secured, free promo downloads, and KU page-reads boost. Full definitions are still pending — see proof-audit.json.

plans.a: Varies by plan — see the current pricing page for the full feature list per tier.

Yes — you can upgrade or downgrade whenever you'd like. When you do, we take your current ad spend into account and apply it as available credit toward the new plan, so nothing you've already paid for is wasted.

plans.q: What happens after a commitment ends?
plans.a: We hand over everything — every video created, account information, and all related assets — via a secure transfer method, so nothing gets lost. In practice, most of this is already available to you throughout the engagement: every gallery of content we make is public to you as the author, presented in your progress-report document/link.
Longer commitments are prepaid savings, not a cancellation trap. The system has more time to compound, and predictable planning lets us offer better economics.

delivery.q: What do I need to provide?
delivery.a: Just a link to your book — or, if you have a backlist, a link to your catalogue. You can also share any planned discount-deal dates so we can plan campaigns around them.

delivery.q: Do I need to appear on camera?
delivery.a: No — you never need to appear on camera.
Depends on plan: 60 videos/month at Spark and Enhanced, 80 at Foundation, 100+ at Starter, Momentum, and Growth.
A dedicated outreach team manages your account day-to-day — reaching out to ARC and reviewer lists on your behalf and making sure everything is running smoothly.

audience.q: Can you work with a brand-new author?
audience.a: Yes — Spark is built for pre-launch or very early-career authors with little to no existing platform.

audience.q: Can you work with a backlist?
audience.a: Yes — Growth is built for authors with an established backlist (3+ books) scaling an existing readership.
All genres. One honest caveat: bigger, higher-volume genres tend to see stronger results than smaller genres or subgenres, simply because there's a larger pool of readers to reach.

commitment.q: What happens if Atomic Shelf does not deliver?
commitment.a: If impressions, click-throughs, or an entire agreed deliverable come back at zero despite the work being carried out as scheduled, that's a non-delivery event and you're entitled to a refund of that specific undelivered portion — you have 21 days from the end of the campaign cycle to report it.

commitment.q: What does the commitment/guarantee actually cover?
commitment.a: It covers the specific work committed to under your plan — production, listing optimization, ARC campaigns, preorder setup, reporting, and communication. It does not cover a specific sales number, rank, or viral outcome.

commitment.q: What happens if the strategy needs to change?
commitment.a: If results are tracking below the expected range but the work was delivered, we review the account, diagnose what's driving it, adjust the approach, and keep working through the rest of the cycle — that's not a refund event, it's the time-based remedy.
